(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১) Which one is most common gastric neoplasm?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Gastric carcinoma (adenocarcinoma) is the most common malignant neoplasm of the stomach and is the most common gastric neoplasm among the given options.

  • Carcinoma → most common gastric neoplasm

  • Polyps → benign mucosal lesions

  • Sarcoma → rare

  • Adenoma → benign glandular tumor

Exam pearl:
“Most common gastric neoplasm = Carcinoma (adenocarcinoma).”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ২) Carcinomas in the............ colon tend to be annular lesions that produce ‘napkin ring’?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Carcinomas of the distal colon, particularly the left/descending and sigmoid colon, commonly grow circumferentially around the bowel lumen, producing an annular “napkin-ring” or “apple-core” lesion.

  • Distal/left-sided colon → annular, constricting (“napkin-ring”) lesion

  • Proximal/right-sided colon → more often exophytic/polypoid mass

Exam pearl:
“Left-sided colon carcinoma → annular/napkin-ring lesion → obstruction.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৩) Peptic ulcers are........ ulcerative lesion of GIT?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
A peptic ulcer is a chronic ulcerative lesion of the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly affecting the stomach and duodenum.

It results from an imbalance between mucosal protective mechanisms and acid-peptic injury, with common causes including H. pylori infection and NSAID use.

Exam pearl:
“Peptic ulcer = Chronic ulcerative lesion of GIT.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৪) Which is non epithelial tumor of stomach?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Leiomyoma is a non-epithelial (mesenchymal) tumor arising from smooth muscle of the stomach.

  • Leiomyoma → non-epithelial/mesenchymal tumor

  • Adenoma → epithelial tumor

  • Adenocarcinoma → epithelial malignant tumor

  • Carcinoid (neuroendocrine tumor) → epithelial/neuroendocrine origin

Exam pearl:
“Stomach non-epithelial tumor → Leiomyoma.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৫) Which is the most common site of metastatic lesions of carcinoma colon?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
The liver is the most common site of metastasis from colorectal carcinoma because venous drainage from the colon (via the portal venous system) carries tumor cells directly to the liver.

  • Colon → portal vein → liver → most common metastatic site

  • Lungs → another important site

  • Brain and thyroid → much less common

Exam pearl:
“Colorectal carcinoma → most common metastasis = Liver.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৬) Which organ is mostly affected in PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) most commonly affects the duodenum, particularly the first part of the duodenum (duodenal bulb).

  • Duodenum → commonest site

  • Stomach → also commonly affected

  • Esophagus → uncommon

  • Meckel’s diverticulum → may rarely develop peptic ulceration due to ectopic gastric mucosa

Exam pearl:
“PUD → Duodenum (especially 1st part) is the commonest site.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৭) Which environmental factor is present in most cases of intestinal type carcinoma?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
The intestinal type of gastric carcinoma is strongly associated with chronic Helicobacter pylori infection. Persistent infection can cause chronic gastritis → atrophy → intestinal metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma.

  • H. pylori → major environmental risk factor for intestinal-type gastric carcinoma

  • Smoked/salted foods → associated dietary risk factors

  • Cigarette smoking → increases gastric cancer risk

  • NSAIDs → not a major risk factor for gastric carcinoma

Exam pearl:
“Intestinal-type gastric carcinoma → H. pylori + chronic atrophic gastritis + intestinal metaplasia.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৮) Which is not a macroscopic growth pattern in gastric carcinoma?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
The recognized macroscopic growth patterns of gastric carcinoma include:

  • Exophytic → projects into the gastric lumen

  • Flat → relatively superficial lesion

  • Excavated → ulcerated/depressed lesion

“Irregular” is not considered a standard macroscopic growth pattern/classification.

Exam pearl:
“Gastric carcinoma growth patterns → Exophytic + Flat + Excavated.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ৯) A gastric carcinoma can be termed as advanced when it has been extended below......?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
A gastric carcinoma is termed advanced gastric cancer when the tumor has invaded beyond the mucosa into the submucosa or deeper layers.

  • Early gastric cancer → confined to mucosa or submucosa, regardless of lymph-node involvement.

  • Advanced gastric cancer → extends beyond the submucosa (into muscularis propria or deeper).

Important correction:
Strictly speaking, the statement “advanced when extended below submucosa” is more accurate than “below submucosa” as an answer choice. Therefore, submucosa is the threshold separating early from advanced disease only in some simplified exam formulations, but by standard definition, advanced gastric cancer invades beyond the submucosa.

Exam pearl:
“Early gastric cancer = mucosa/submucosa; Advanced gastric cancer = beyond submucosa.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১০) Which is the major factor in pathogenesis of PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
H. pylori infection is a major etiological factor in the pathogenesis of peptic ulcer disease (PUD). It damages the gastric mucosal defense and promotes inflammation, making the mucosa more susceptible to acid-peptic injury.

Other factors:

  • NSAIDs → inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and impair mucosal protection; also a major cause of PUD.

  • Cigarette smoking → increases ulcer risk and impairs healing.

  • Stress → can contribute, especially in critically ill patients, but is not the major cause of ordinary PUD.

Exam pearl:
“Major causes of PUD → H. pylori + NSAIDs.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১১) Which is the most common malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Among the given options, colorectal adenocarcinoma is the most common malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract.

  • Colon → adenocarcinoma is the predominant GI malignancy

  • Stomach → adenocarcinoma is common but less frequent

  • Cholangiocarcinoma → relatively rare

  • Barrett’s esophagus → premalignant condition, not a malignancy itself

Exam pearl:
“Most common GI tract malignancy → Colorectal adenocarcinoma.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১২) Which type of anemia occurs in colorectal carcinoma?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Colorectal carcinoma commonly causes chronic occult blood loss from the gastrointestinal tract, leading to iron deficiency anemia.

  • Right-sided colon cancer → iron deficiency anemia may be an important presenting feature

  • Chronic microscopic bleeding → gradual iron depletion

  • Typical findings → low Hb, low serum ferritin, low MCV (microcytic hypochromic anemia)

Exam pearl:
“Colorectal carcinoma + occult GI blood loss → Iron deficiency anemia.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৩) Which blood group is mostly affected by PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
People with blood group O have a higher risk of developing duodenal peptic ulcer disease (PUD) compared with other ABO blood groups.

  • Blood group O → increased risk of duodenal ulcer

  • Blood group A → relatively more associated with gastric carcinoma

Exam pearl:
“PUD/duodenal ulcer → Blood group O.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৪) How many zones are demonstrable in peptic ulcer?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
A chronic peptic ulcer classically shows 4 zones histologically, from the lumen/deep surface downward:

  1. Necrotic zone – superficial layer of necrotic debris

  2. Inflammatory exudate zone – acute inflammatory cells and fibrin

  3. Granulation tissue zone – healing tissue with new capillaries and fibroblasts

  4. Fibrous scar zone – deepest layer of dense fibrous tissue

Exam pearl:
“Peptic ulcer histology = 4 zones: Necrosis → Inflammation → Granulation tissue → Fibrous scar.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৫) Which is true about lesion of classic peptic ulcer?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
A classic chronic peptic ulcer typically has all of these features:

  • Round to oval in shape

  • Sharply punched-out mucosal defect

  • Smooth, clean base due to digestion of the tissue by gastric acid and pepsin

Therefore, all of the above are true.

Exam pearl:
“Chronic peptic ulcer → round/oval + punched-out + smooth, clean base.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৬) Which is not true about colorectal carcinoma?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.option1: incidence peaks at 60 to 70 years of age
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.option2: less than 20% of cases occur before age 50
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.option3: females are affected slightly more often than male
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.option4: aspirin or other NSAIDs have a protective effect
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
The statement that is not true is “females are affected slightly more often than males.”

In fact, colorectal carcinoma is slightly more common in males than females.

The other statements are true:

  • Incidence peaks around 60–70 years

  • <20% of cases occur before age 50 (traditional teaching)

  • Aspirin/NSAIDs can have a protective effect by reducing colorectal neoplasia risk.

Exam pearl:
“Colorectal carcinoma → slightly more common in males.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৭) Which part of stomach is commonly affected in PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
When peptic ulcer disease affects the stomach, the antrum—particularly the lesser curvature near the incisura angularis—is a common site.

  • Antrum → common site

  • Fundus → uncommon

  • Pylorus → less common

  • Cardia → uncommon

Exam pearl:
“Gastric PUD → antrum/lesser curvature.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৮) What is the background of development of PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Chronic gastritis, particularly H. pylori-associated chronic gastritis, provides an important background for the development of peptic ulcer disease (PUD).

  • Chronic gastritis → mucosal inflammation and impaired mucosal defense → PUD

  • H. pylori infection is a major cause of chronic gastritis and PUD.

Exam pearl:
“Background of PUD → Chronic gastritis.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ১৯) Which is fundamental to the pathogenesis of PUD?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
The fundamental mechanism in peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is an imbalance between aggressive factors (gastric acid and pepsin) and mucosal defensive mechanisms.

Gastric hyperacidity increases acid-peptic injury and contributes to ulcer formation.

  • Gastric hyperacidity → fundamental pathogenic factor

  • Stress → aggravating factor

  • Irregular food habit → not a primary cause

  • Spicy food → may aggravate symptoms but does not directly cause PUD

Exam pearl:
“PUD pathogenesis = Acid-peptic injury > mucosal defense.”

(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.question: ২০) Sites of PUD excludes......?
(Pathology) Peptic ulcer disease, Carcin.exp:
Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) occurs in areas exposed to gastric acid and pepsin, such as:

  • Stomach

  • Duodenum

  • Lower esophagus (rare, usually associated with acid reflux)

The colon is not a site of PUD.

Exam pearl:
“PUD sites → Stomach + Duodenum ± lower esophagus; Colon = not a site.”
